gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many 4.5-hour rounds each under-$300 watch gets per charge, or how often a golfer who plays twice a week has to charge it. From Garmin's own manual figures: vívoactive 5/6 gets 3.8 rounds (all-satellite, 17 h) or 4.7 rounds (GPS-only, 21 h) and needs a charge about every 6.0–6.6 days. The Approach S44 gets 3.3 rounds and needs a charge about every 5.4 days.
standout_why: I compared against panxis.com (golf-watch-battery-claimed-lived), cubicalgolfer.com/best-golf-gps-watch-under-300, garmin.com en-US 'What's the best Garmin golf watch for me?', and Garmin's S44/S50 and vívoactive 5 press releases. Panxis has the only rounds math, and it covers just the Approach S44, S50 and S70 plus Shot Scope ('a 15-hour rating covers roughly 2.5 to 3 such rounds'). It does not cover the vívoactive 5/6, the fitness-tracker candidates. Cubicalgolfer gives undefined '3 rounds'/'5 rounds' figures for the S42 and S12, not the S44 or vívoactive, with no round length. Garmin's blog and press releases give hours or days only. No page combines GPS hours with smartwatch days into how often a twice-a-week golfer charges. ChatGPT's answers compared smartwatch days only (11 vs 10) and footnoted that this is 'not continuous golf GPS use'.
decides: This confirms the vívoactive 5 over the Approach S44 for this shopper. On Garmin's own like-for-like all-satellite figures, the vívoactive 5 lasts longer on the course (3.8 vs 3.3 rounds) and between charges (6.0 vs 5.4 days for a twice-a-week golfer). It also has the wrist heart rate and sleep tracking the S44 lacks. So the S44's golf-first pitch does not come with a battery advantage. The vívoactive 6 has the same battery figures as the vívoactive 5, so battery gives no reason to pay more for it. The Approach S12 lasts far longer (6.7 rounds; about 17.5 days at two rounds a week) but is not a fitness tracker. I could not compute the Amazfit Balance 2 from a page I opened, so this angle cannot rank it against the Garmins.
